title: Dice Roll Simulation
statement: Each roll of a die shows one of the faces 1 to 6. A sequence of rolls is allowed when no face `i` appears more than `rollMax[i - 1]` times back to back anywhere in it (so `rollMax[0]` caps runs of face 1 and `rollMax[5]` caps runs of face 6). Count the allowed sequences made of exactly `n` rolls, where two sequences are different if they disagree in at least one position. The count can be huge, so return it modulo `10^9 + 7`.
notes:
## Intuition

Listing all 6^n sequences is hopeless. What matters about a partial sequence is only how it ends: which face came last and how many times in a row. So group the sequences by that ending, `dp[face][run]`, and update the groups one roll at a time.

## Approach

1. After the first roll there is one sequence per face, each ending in a run of 1: `dp[face][1] = 1`.
2. For every later roll, add up `endsWith[face]`, the sequences ending in each face, and their sum `total`.
3. Rolling a different face from the last one starts a fresh run: `next[face][1] = total - endsWith[face]`.
4. Rolling the same face again lengthens its run: `next[face][run] = dp[face][run - 1]`, but only while `run <= rollMax[face]`, so runs that are too long never appear.
5. After `n` rolls, add up every cell of `dp`. Keep every sum modulo `10^9 + 7`.

## Example 1, step by step

`n = 2`, `rollMax = [1, 1, 2, 2, 2, 3]`. After roll 1 each face has `dp[face][1] = 1`, so `total = 6`. On roll 2, every face gets `next[face][1] = 6 - 1 = 5` (30 sequences). Faces 3 to 6 allow a run of 2, so each gets `next[face][2] = 1` (4 more); faces 1 and 2 do not. The answer is `30 + 4 = 34`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n · 6 · 15): each roll touches every (face, run) cell a constant number of times.
- Space: O(6 · 16): only the current and next tables are kept.

## Pitfalls

- `total - endsWith[face]` can go negative after taking remainders; add `MOD` before the final `%`.
- `rollMax` is indexed from 0 for face 1; mixing up the offset shifts every limit.
- The first roll fills the table directly, so the loop starts at `roll = 2`; running it `n` times would count sequences of `n + 1` rolls.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `MOD` | the modulus `10^9 + 7` |
| `dp[face][run]` | sequences so far ending with exactly `run` copies of `face` |
| `roll` | how many rolls the sequences have after this step |
| `endsWith[face]` | sequences so far whose last roll is `face` |
| `total` | all sequences so far |
| `next` | the table after one more roll |
| `answer` | sum of every cell after `n` rolls |
